speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe the appearance of the rash in detail, such as whether it is flat, raised, or blistered, and when exactly did it first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash spread from the face to the trunk and extremities over several days, which is characteristic of erythema infectiosum. Do you recall if her cheeks looked bright red or "slapped" before the rash spread to her body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy, mildly pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, along with preceding mild viral symptoms, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum
